subject: Nariway Daily Check-in - 2026-08-17
html:
Nariway Daily Check-in

17 August 2026

Needs your attention / action today

  • Reply and log as Query A responses land. The response window opened this week and the Qwoted Intelligence Log is still empty (first responses expected now). Use the invite/triage/hold templates and log every substantive reply, not just the interview-worthy ones.
  • Send the Vogel outreach. Ruth Fine first, then the four museum inquiries (SIU/Sharp, Seattle, the High, Academy Art Museum). Both drafts are ready and waiting in the afterlife file's outreach section — they only go out when you send them.
  • One fact only you know: does your bio say "more than 100 museums" or "hundreds of museums"? website.md and positioning.md now disagree — flagged by both this week's QA and hygiene sweeps. A one-line reply picks the true figure so the drift can be fixed.
  • Confirm your work-log hours for Aug 12 through 16 (five days, all still draft estimates) — needed for the tax record.

Today I learned

The report's central claim finally has a real number behind it: 13 of 13 non-founder-sole institutions survived their founder, versus 10 of 13 founder-sole ones (77%), out of 26 testable cases. Every prior run had asserted "governance beats endowment" case-by-case, in prose, as new examples arrived. This run instead pulled the coded fields directly from all 50 case files and restricted to the only sub-sample the methodology says is honestly testable. The asterisk makes it more credible, not less: the 3 founder-sole "failures" aren't one pattern — two are death-triggered governance collapses like Terra, the third is a structurally different living-founder closure (Fisher Landau) that isn't really the same failure mode at all. Source: cases/report-dataset.md, Pattern 14.

What changed, and what it means

  • Query A is live and the response window has opened. This is the actual test of everything built so far — not the post itself, a real response turning into a conversation.
  • The case dataset hit its target breadth, 50 of 50. Future research runs shift entirely to depth: primary-source verification once WebFetch unblocks, and cross-case analysis like today's governance table.
  • WebFetch stayed blocked for an eighth consecutive research run. Primary verification is still stalled; this run narrowed three backlog contradictions via WebSearch instead of resolving them outright.
  • A vault hygiene sweep fixed 8 issues automatically today — broken links, a stale case count, drifted case frontmatter — with nothing critical. Nothing needed from you there beyond the museum-count call above.
  • The CFO's Monday drift flag is only half-answered. Query A did post that evening, but the first Substack Note is still unposted — the CMO steward has now flagged that same gap three days running, and this week's QA pass found all four drafted Notes end on a soft summary line rather than a concrete fact, so they need a rewrite before they're postable, not just a publish click.

Where we stand

The one-million goal's biggest unknown — will anyone actually pay — gets its first real data point this week: Query A is live and the response window is open now. The flagship report has reached its target breadth and its central claim now has an actual number behind it instead of a prose assertion, but the dollar test is still ahead of the research test, and the Substack Note that was supposed to make Artobiography look alive to a first respondent still hasn't posted.

Work log

Aug 12–16 hours are still logged as draft estimates — reply to confirm or correct them so the tax record stays current.
